question: What defines a cross-sectional research design regarding time?

options.A: Data is gathered retrospectively from old hospital files
options.B: Data is collected at one specific point in time
options.C: Data is collected over a period of ten years
options.D: Data is collected prospectively after a clinical intervention

explanation: Cross-sectional studies examine a population at a single, defined moment, acting like a snapshot. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is a cross-sectional study likened to a photographic snapshot?

options.A: It requires expensive high-resolution camera equipment
options.B: It produces visual graphs instead of statistical tables
options.C: It captures a population status at one moment
options.D: It permanently freezes cellular tissue for laboratory analysis

explanation: The snapshot analogy highlights that the design captures variables at one single point without showing past or future changes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which feature is always absent in a cross-sectional study?

options.B: Researcher manipulation of the study variable
options.D: Use of structured questionnaires or surveys

explanation: Cross-sectional studies are purely observational, meaning researchers do not administer treatments or manipulate conditions. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h2)

question: When is a cross-sectional study classified as analytical rather than purely descriptive?

options.A: When it excludes all quantitative data in favor of audio interviews
options.B: When the researcher introduces a new nursing care protocol
options.C: When it follows the patient cohort for at least five years
options.D: When it examines statistical associations between exposures and outcomes

explanation: Analytical cross-sectional studies go beyond simple counts to test relationships between risk factors and health conditions. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the very first step when planning a cross-sectional study?

options.A: Entering numerical data into computer software
options.C: Publishing the final article in a nursing journal
options.D: Applying for ethical clearance from the hospital board

explanation: Every research project must begin with a clear research question that guides the population selection and data gathering methods. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h3)

question: A nurse researcher wants to study hypertension prevalence in a rural market. What should be done immediately after defining the population?

options.C: Begin treating patients with antihypertensive drugs

explanation: Determining the sample size follows population definition to ensure enough participants are recruited for valid statistical power. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h3)

question: What data collection method is often best for populations with low literacy levels?
explanation: Interviews allow researchers to read questions aloud and clarify meanings for participants who might struggle with written forms. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why must data collection instruments be both valid and reliable in cross-sectional research?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any statistical analysis later
options.B: To guarantee the research receives international grant funding
options.C: To reduce the total number of survey questions by half
options.D: To ensure they accurately measure what is intended consistently

explanation: Validity and reliability guarantee that the single snapshot of data collected actually reflects true clinical realities. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which statistical measure is commonly used to report disease frequency in cross-sectional studies?
explanation: Cross-sectional studies measure existing cases at one point, which gives the prevalence of the condition rather than its new incidence. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is it incorrect to claim causation from a statistically significant cross-sectional association?

options.A: Statistical software packages cannot calculate causal pathways
options.B: Exposure and outcome are measured at the exact same time
options.C: Ethics committees forbid the use of regression models
options.D: Sample sizes in cross-sectional studies are always too small

explanation: Simultaneous measurement makes it impossible to know whether the exposure preceded the outcome or vice versa. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is a major advantage of cross-sectional research designs?

options.A: They require no ethical clearance from institutional boards
options.B: They track patient health outcomes over many decades
options.C: They are relatively quick and cost-effective to conduct
options.D: They prove definitive cause and effect relationships

explanation: Because data is gathered all at once without follow-up periods, these studies save both time and financial resources. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a disadvantage of cross-sectional studies?

options.A: High susceptibility to loss to follow-up over time
options.B: Vulnerability to recall bias from survey participants
options.D: Inability to establish clear temporal sequence or causation

explanation: Loss to follow-up is a problem in longitudinal or cohort studies, not cross-sectional studies where participants are contacted only once. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h6)

question: A Nigerian nurse manager needs a quick assessment of ward supply shortages to present to the hospital board next week. Which study design is most appropriate?
explanation: A cross-sectional survey delivers rapid data necessary for immediate administrative planning and resource allocation. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h7)

question: How do cross-sectional studies directly support community health nursing in Nigeria?

options.A: By identifying local disease burdens to target public health interventions
options.B: By proving genetic causes of inherited tropical diseases
options.C: By following individual patients from birth until old age
options.D: By testing new surgical techniques in major teaching hospitals

explanation: Community health nurses use prevalence data from cross-sectional surveys to plan effective outreach and educational programs. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h7)
